selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What small food is used as the main example in this passage?
questions.answer: An apple.

questions.question: According to the passage, who alone can make that fruit and give it to people as real food?
questions.answer: Allah, the Creator of everything.

questions.question: What big things in the world are mentioned to show this great power?
questions.answer: The seasons, day and night, and the earth moving.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect one apple to those very big things?
questions.answer: Because bringing one fruit needs control over the whole world around it.

questions.question: What does the passage say is found on one apple and also on other fruits, plants, and animals?
questions.answer: Signs of wisdom, mercy, and one Maker.

questions.question: If the same special signs are on many living things, what does that help us understand?
questions.answer: They all come from the same Creator.

questions.question: How is the earth described in relation to the apple?
questions.answer: Like its garden.

questions.question: How is the whole universe described in relation to the apple?
questions.answer: Like a great tree or factory for it.

questions.question: What do spring and summer do for the fruit in the passage?
questions.answer: They are the times when it grows and ripens.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
questions.answer: Even one fruit shows Allah’s oneness and power over all creation.

questions.question: What gift to a person does the passage talk about first?
questions.answer: Giving a person an apple for food.

questions.question: Is that gift shown as a small, easy thing or as something needing great power?
questions.answer: It is shown as needing great power.

questions.question: What moving parts of the world are named in the passage?
questions.answer: The seasons, the days, the nights, and the earth.

questions.question: Why are people on earth called needy guests in the passage?
questions.answer: Because they need food given to them.

questions.question: What idea does the passage teach by saying fruits of different times are brought close to people?
questions.answer: Allah arranges the world so people can receive their food.

questions.question: What does the passage say about apples and other fruits being alike in an important way?
questions.answer: They all carry the same signs from their Maker.

questions.question: What does that sameness tell us about who made them?
questions.answer: One Lord made them all.

questions.question: Besides fruits, what other living things are named with them?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: Why must the Maker of an apple also be the Maker of the earth?
questions.answer: Because the apple depends on the earth and the whole system around it.

questions.question: What does every fruit become, according to the last sentence?
questions.answer: A sign that points to Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What is one apple called for a human being in this passage?
questions.answer: Real provision or sustenance.

questions.question: What does the passage say must happen in the world for that provision to reach people?
questions.answer: The world must be run in an ordered way.

questions.question: Which repeating changes are mentioned as part of that order?
questions.answer: The changing seasons and the turning of day and night.

questions.question: What picture is used for the earth in motion?
questions.answer: A ship carrying loads.
